successors.note: The Congress Poland dossier carries the Kingdom itself to 1915.

capitals.name: Warsaw
capitals.note: 'The capital was located in Warsaw'; the rising began there on 29 November 1830 and Warsaw capitulated on the night of 7 September 1831.

correction.text: the shape unchanged but only for 1830-1831 (Congress Poland in the hands of the insurgents); from 1832 it is Russian again

keyframe_review.note: 113,460 km2 (490 cells) against 128,500 km2 for the Kingdom (Congress Poland page), ratio 0.88, within the factor of two; 471 of the cells lie in modern Poland and 18 in Lithuania (the Augustów land), the same land as Congress Poland, and Cliopatria's Russian Empire row has exactly these cells missing in 1830-1833. The shape is right for the Kingdom but not for the years: the November Uprising page ends the fighting in 1831 ('On 5 October 1831 ... over 20,000 men crossed the Prussian frontier'), and the Organic Statute of 1832 made the land 'an integral part of the Russian Empire'. Years only: use 1830-1831; the Russian Empire row should have the land back from 1832.

region.text: the Kingdom of Poland, from Warsaw

ledger.note: 29 November 1830: the November Uprising begins in Warsaw. 'The uprising began on 29 November 1830 in Warsaw'; cadets under Piotr Wysocki attacked the Belweder Palace and Grand Duke Constantine escaped. The Sejm dethroned Nicholas I on 25 January 1831 and a national government under Adam Jerzy Czartoryski was set up on 29 January. The page does not say what land the insurgents held; the region is the Kingdom (Congress Poland page: 128,500 km2).

November 1830: the Kingdom of Poland leaves Russian rule. Grand Duke Constantine escaped from Warsaw on the first night (my reading: Russian rule in the Kingdom lapsed with it); the Act of Dethronization of 25 January 1831 was 'equivalent to a declaration of war on Russia'. The page does not map the land held.

region.text: the Kingdom of Poland, the theatre of the war

ledger.note: February 1831: the Russian army fights its way into the Kingdom. The first battle on the page is 'Stoczek, 14 February 1831: a Polish tactical success', then Olszynka Grochowska on 25 February 1831 (about 40,000 Poles against 60,000 Russians); the page does not date the Russian crossing of the border.

5 October 1831: the Polish army lays down its arms. Wola fell to Paskevich on 6 September 1831, Krukowiecki capitulated on the night of 7 September, and 'the remaining Polish army of over 20,000 men crossed the Prussian frontier' on 5 October 1831 and laid down arms at Brodnica.

October 1831: the Kingdom is back under Russia. Organised resistance collapsed in October 1831; the Organic Statute of 1832 then made Poland 'an integral part of the Russian Empire' (Warsaw a garrison city, its university closed). Cliopatria keeps the 'Poles' shape to 1833 and has Russia back in 1834.
October 1831: the insurgent state ends. The remaining army crossed into Prussia on 5 October 1831; the Congress Poland page says the uprising 'was crushed after an 11-month campaign'.

wars.name: November Uprising

zones.text: the Kingdom of Poland and, in the spread of the rising, parts of Lithuania, Belarus and right-bank Ukraine

wars.outcome: The rising was crushed after an 11-month campaign: Warsaw fell on 6-8 September 1831, the army crossed into Prussia on 5 October 1831; the Organic Statute of 1832 abolished the Kingdom's constitution, army and legislative assembly. Austria and Prussia took 'a position of benevolent neutrality towards Russia'.
wars.note: The infobox lists the theatre as 'Poland, Lithuania, Belarus and right-bank Ukraine' and the text says attempts were made to rouse Volhynia, Podolia, Samogitia and Lithuania; the pages say nothing about land held outside the Kingdom, so none is drawn.

certainty.note: A war-time territory: the Kingdom of Poland's 1815 frontier, held until the Russian advance of 1831.

notes:
Written for batch eu-20-l (2 pages; budget 1-2). The Cliopatria row 'Poles' (1830-1833, one shape of 113,460 km2) is the Kingdom of Poland (Congress Poland) taken out of the Russian Empire row for four years: the Russian Empire dossier already records a loss to 'poles' in 1830 and a gain in 1834 (bridging). The November Uprising page and the Congress Poland page put the end in 1831 (the army crossed into Prussia on 5 October 1831; the Organic Statute of 1832), so the shape's 1832-1833 years belong to Russia: the Russian Empire dossier should end its 'poles' loss in 1831/1832.

NOT SETTLED. (1) The territory the insurgents actually held: the pages give no map, so the whole Kingdom is used for the whole war (the Russian army entered in February 1831; the page does not date the crossing). (2) The Lithuanian, Volhynian, Podolian and Samogitian risings are not drawn. (3) The Free City of Kraków is not mentioned on either page. (4) The dossier's name, type (rebel) and wikipedia title ('November Uprising', not Cliopatria's 'Polish people') are mine; the Congress Poland dossier (batch eu-20) calls the same body 'Polish National Government' (a string counterpart); it should use this slug. (5) The head of state: the page names only Adam Jerzy Czartoryski as head of the national government of 29 January 1831; no ruler strip.

GAZETTEER NAMES: none needed (the Cliopatria shape is used).
